cues.text: Before drawing anything, set the units in Model Settings.
Unit name is the suffix shown on every measurement. Type cm.
Unit size says how long one model unit is. One unit, one centimetre.
Grid size is the snap spacing, in units. Five gives a 5 cm grid.
Good. Now move over the grid. The coloured axes on the cursor show where it snaps.
Start with the table top. Choose Rectangle.
Click two grid points, 60 cm apart in each direction.
Uh oh, nothing to snap to up in the air. Press T to add an axis helper.
Its blue axis points straight up and snaps at every grid step.
Push/Pull: pick the corner, then a point one step up the helper.
Nice! Make Object keeps this part from merging with what we draw next.
Now lift the top. Move: pick its corner, then a point up the helper.
Goooood. Next, one leg: a small square under the corner of the top.
Pull it up until the cursor snaps to the corner underneath the top.
Make it an object too, so all four legs share one definition.
Move Copy repeats it. Pick the leg's corner, then a grid point 55 cm along.
You can also type a distance. Pick a start, aim, type 55 and press Enter.
Niiiice! Clear Guides removes the helper once it has done its job.
Right-drag to orbit and check the result from another side.
Cool. That's the whole method: set units, snap to the grid, climb with helpers.
